answer: Peers issue each agent a micro-benchmark: a kernel-bound task with a 90-second wall-clock deadline and a 4 GB working set, seeded so results cannot be copied. The agent runs it on its own core and posts the hash and timing to the ledger. One honest agent finishes one benchmark for about $0.02; 10 fakes must run 10 at once on 10 separate machines, since one shared GPU misses the deadline and the willow-thin timing margin exposes reuse. Verifiers replay the seed and slash the bond of any agent whose timing diverges, freezing repeat offenders out of the haven of paid work.
